derivation.claim: Use the actual source reduction, then fix k=2.
derivation.details: Normalize the Planar 3SAT input by deleting unused variables and tautological clauses, coalescing repeated literals, and resolving an empty clause directly if needed. Each retained clause has q in {1,2,3}. In an embedding, each variable occurrence gets a distinct four-node segment x(j),a(j),not-x(j),b(j); ring weights alternate k,k,1,1. A clause vertex connects by a weight-1 edge to the corresponding occurrence literal. A separate 2k-cycle of weight-k edges is used for every b vertex and every clause; b has k-1 external weight-1 links to distinct even special vertices, a q-literal clause has k+1-q such links. This is exactly the source construction, not an assumption about arbitrary planar bipartite inputs.
derivation.evidence: Asahiro printed pp.15-17, Theorem13 and Figure6.

derivation.claim: Every load-at-most-k solution saturates each special ring internally.
derivation.details: The 2k ring edges contribute total outgoing load 2k^2 to 2k ring vertices. Their combined capacity at threshold k is exactly 2k^2. Thus each ring vertex has internal outgoing load exactly k, equivalently exactly one outgoing ring edge. The ring is directed consistently, and every weight-1 attachment must point from the outside vertex into the ring. This supplies b with forced outgoing attachment load k-1.

derivation.claim: Every load-at-most-k solution orients each variable cycle consistently.
derivation.details: At a literal vertex its two cycle weights are k and 1, so both cannot leave; at a vertex a both cycle weights are k; at b the two cycle weights are 1 and 1 but attachment load k-1 forbids both leaving. Each cycle vertex therefore has at most one outgoing cycle edge. Since the number of cycle edges equals its number of vertices, every vertex has exactly one outgoing cycle edge, so the cycle has one of its two consistent directions. These two directions swap which literal nodes have cycle load 1 (true) and k (false), yielding one consistent truth value per variable.

derivation.claim: The source threshold equivalence is genuinely two-sided.
derivation.details: For a satisfying assignment, direct each variable ring accordingly, direct special rings cyclically, and point attachments into them. For each clause choose one true occurrence, point its edge from literal to clause, and point the other clause edges outward. A true literal has cycle load 1 and at most one additional outgoing occurrence edge, hence load <=2<=k; a false literal remains at k; b has load (k-1)+1=k; a has load k; a clause has k outgoing unit edges. Conversely, under threshold k the special and variable constraints just proved hold. A clause has k+1 incident unit edges and all its special links leave it, so some literal edge enters it. Its tail cannot be a false node already at cycle load k; hence it names a true literal. All clauses are satisfied. Thus SAT iff OPT<=k; integrality gives UNSAT implies OPT>=k+1. In particular k=2 gives the required 2-versus-3 gap.

derivation.claim: At k=2 the exact original graph class includes every property needed for the bridge.
derivation.details: The graph is simple and loopless: all occurrence and special vertices are fresh, cycles have lengths at least four, links have distinct endpoints, and each occurrence has one clause edge. The inherited planar embedding replaces variable discs by occurrence rings in cyclic order and places each own special gadget in a small incident face. It is bipartite with one part containing all a,b,clause and odd special vertices and the other containing literal and even special vertices. Degrees: each literal <=3, a=2, b=2+(k-1)=3, each q-clause=q+(k+1-q)=3, special vertices <=3. Thus Delta<=3, and all weights are in {1,2}. A three-literal clause has zero special attachment edges at k=2; its unused special 4-cycle may be kept as a disconnected harmless component.

derivation.claim: Produce an explicit valid scheduling instance and preserve all feasible costs.
derivation.details: Let M=V(G), J=E(G). Set p[v,e]=w(e) at each endpoint v of e and infinity at every other machine. Every job has exactly two eligible machines, equal positive finite processing times in {1,2}, and every machine has at most three eligible jobs. Explicit matrix size |V||E| is polynomial. Map an MMO directed edge u->v to assignment of its job to tail u; conversely orient a job from its assigned endpoint to its other endpoint. These are inverse maps preserving each machine load and hence makespan and OPT for all schedules, not merely at threshold 2. Page counts incoming rather than outgoing weights; reversing every arc reconciles notation. Infinity remains an eligibility marker, so no extra eligibility edges are introduced.

derivation.claim: The exact job-intersection graph is L(G) and has no ordinary diamond subgraph.
derivation.details: Two job vertices are adjacent precisely when the corresponding original edges share an endpoint, hence the graph is the line graph. In a simple triangle-free graph, three pairwise-intersecting distinct edges either share one common endpoint or form an original triangle. Bipartiteness excludes the latter, so every line-graph triangle is the clique at one original vertex. A diamond subgraph has two triangles sharing two line-graph vertices, i.e. two original edges. Simplicity forces those two edges to share exactly one endpoint v. Both triples, hence all four distinct original edges of the diamond, would have to meet v, contrary to degree <=3. This excludes non-induced diamonds as required, including potential K4s.

derivation.claim: The whole target hardness, including every fixed approximation factor, follows.
derivation.details: Compose Planar 3SAT -> G -> the explicit processing matrix. Every output is simultaneously in the target diamondless class and has <=3 eligible jobs per machine; YES has OPT<=2 and NO has OPT>=3. Therefore the target promise distinction is NP-hard. For any fixed 1<=c<3/2, a polynomial c-approximation would give YES cost <=2c<3, while every NO schedule costs >=3. Testing output cost <3 decides Planar 3SAT. Since all finite weights are constants, numerical encoding and pseudo-polynomial time cannot erase the gap. At c=3/2 the strict separation disappears, consistently with Page Theorem2/Corollary3.

whole_result_assessment.verdict: Mathematically accepted, unconditional transfer in the usual P-versus-NP hardness convention; whole_result is justified.
whole_result_assessment.whole_result: The k=2 actual Theorem13 reduction, with its explicitly proved subcubic simple bipartite structure and endpoint assignment bijection, establishes the entire target gap and every fixed c<3/2 approximation lower bound.
whole_result_assessment.not_merely_contribution: The proof pays both threshold directions, structural membership, full cost-preserving model mapping, polynomial encoding and approximation quantifiers. There is no remaining mathematical step needed for this target.

boundaries: Do not use planar bipartite graph membership alone: K1,4 is simple planar bipartite but its line graph is K4 and contains a diamond subgraph.
Do not generalize the diamondless bridge to source k>=3. Then b and clause vertices have degree k+1>=4, yielding at least a K4 in the task intersection graph.
Do not equate diamondless with induced-diamond-free: K4 is induced-diamond-free but fails diamondless.
Do not identify the original machine graph with the task-intersection graph. Bipartiteness of G does not imply bipartiteness or triangle-freeness of L(G).

The transfer only needs a restricted assignment subclass with exactly two equal-time eligible machines per job. It proves hardness for the target larger unrelated-machine class, but supplies no algorithm or model equivalence for arbitrary machine-dependent times or eligibility sets.
Do not claim the c=3/2 endpoint is impossible, nor reverse the edge to obtain all-k source hardness from the fixed target gap.
Target assumptions naming its paper At-most-3-SAT(2L) proof are provenance of an alternate proof, not an additional structural restriction which this alternative Planar 3SAT proof must satisfy.
